segments.text: In 1815, a volcano on the other side of the world cancelled summer in Europe. This is the story of the year without a summer.
Mount Tambora, on the island of Sumbawa, erupted with a force ten times greater than Krakatoa. It threw so much ash into the stratosphere that sunlight itself dimmed.
By the following June, snow was falling in New England and crops were failing across France and Germany. Bread riots followed. Nobody yet understood why.
Out of that cold, wet summer came Frankenstein, written by Mary Shelley while trapped indoors by the rain. One eruption, one lost harvest, one monster that never died.
